newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty may have found key NBP support at -1.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Zloty may have found key NBP support at -1.5 pct.

text.p: The Polish zloty may have found key support at -1.5 percent from parity after the central bank intervened to keep the zloty above this level on Thursday.

Dealers said the central bank's small $10 million currency selling intervention in late trade was probably aimed at steadying the zloty above the -1.5 percent level rather than at pushing it up against the currency basket.
"There should be no panic-like trading tomorrow, but players will feel the NBP looking over their shoulders if the zloty heads lower," said Rafal Kaminski, dealer at Pekao SA.
The zloty closed at -1.49/-1.55 percent from parity against Wednesday's close at -1.02/-1.29 percent after the NBP sold dollars around -1.5 percent from parity.
It closed at 3.4535/55 to the dollar, against 3.4360/80 on Wednesday and at 1.8830/50 to the mark, against 1.8770/05.
Dealers said the zloty's near-term range should be between one and 1.5 percent below the parity rate, unless more hot foreign capital flowed into the country.
The zloty eased in early Thursday trade, after rising for the past four trading days, mainly as a result of speculation on the part of Polish banks, dealers said.

The National Bank of Poland further increased its NBP-bill yields at Thursday's auction, with 91-day paper up to 22.99 percent from Wednesday's 22.58. The NBP also upped its 7-day reverse repo rate to 22.90 percent from the previous 22.51.
Analysts said the NBP would not increase official interest rates for the time being, but focus on quickly increasing market rates to cool fast growing domestic demand.
"Through increasing reverse repo rates and NBP-bills yields, the central bank will keep market rates high," said Wlodzimierz Kado, a dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Overnight rates closed at 21.70/22.45 percent against 22.00/22.30 percent at opening and tomorrow/next were at at 22.00/22.35 percent against 22.15/22.55.
